hints: Apply the quadratic formula to w, keeping the complex leading coefficient 2+i.
Simplify the discriminant using (2−i)(2+i)=5 and i²=−1.
For each root, multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate of 4+2i and state both in Cartesian form.
walkthrough:
Identify coefficients in the quadratic equation $(2 + \mathrm{i})w^2 + 4w + (2 - \mathrm{i}) = 0$:
$$a = 2 + \mathrm{i}, \quad b = 4, \quad c = 2 - \mathrm{i}$$

Evaluate the first root taking the minus sign:
$$w_1 = \dfrac{-2 - \mathrm{i}}{2 + \mathrm{i}} = \dfrac{-(2 + \mathrm{i})}{2 + \mathrm{i}} = -1 = -1 + 0\mathrm{i}$$

Evaluate the second root taking the plus sign, multiplying numerator and denominator by the conjugate $2 - \mathrm{i}$:
$$w_2 = \dfrac{-2 + \mathrm{i}}{2 + \mathrm{i}} = \dfrac{(-2 + \mathrm{i})(2 - \mathrm{i})}{(2 + \mathrm{i})(2 - \mathrm{i})}$$
$$\text{Denominator: } 2^2 - \mathrm{i}^2 = 4 - (-1) = 5$$
$$\text{Numerator: } (-2)(2) - (-2)\mathrm{i} + \mathrm{i}(2) - \mathrm{i}^2 = -4 + 2\mathrm{i} + 2\mathrm{i} - (-1) = -4 + 4\mathrm{i} + 1 = -3 + 4\mathrm{i}$$
$$w_2 = \dfrac{-3 + 4\mathrm{i}}{5} = -\dfrac{3}{5} + \dfrac{4}{5}\mathrm{i}$$

State both roots in Cartesian form $x + \mathrm{i}y$:
$$w = -1, \quad w = -\dfrac{3}{5} + \dfrac{4}{5}\mathrm{i}$$
